newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen higher after PPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen higher after PPI.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were seen opening higher after the Producer Price index registered a deeper than expected 0.4 percent decline in February, analysts said. The core rate declined by 0.1 percent.
JIM SOLLOWAY, DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH AT ARGUS RESEARCH.
"We should see a rebound in bond prices and that should help stocks ... both numbers were weaker than expected."
"But current inflation hasn't been the problem, fear of future inflation has been the problem."
BILL MEEHAN, MARKET ANALYST AT PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES,
"We have a negative PPI. We've got the bond market rallying back and the futures are up so we'll pack on a juicy little chunk early in the day."

"The worst fear was that we'd have bad number and prompt the Fed to raise rates. This brings into question Fed action. Can the Fed can move with producer prices actually showing a decline? Still, the Fed does have some ammunition and it's still up in the air whether they will raise rates."
PHILIP ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER AT VALUE LINE'S ASSET MANAGEMENT DIVISION:
"This is a very good number for the market. We're already up a half point in the bond market and I would expect that number to get even stronger."
PETER CARDILLO, DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH, WESTFALIA INVESTMENTS:
"This negates some of yesterday's strong economic data, but I think you have to see that most of this came because of a decline in energy prices."
"I think market will probably regain some of yesterday's losses. We're looking for a fairly strong opening, 15 to 30 (Dow) points on the upside."
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast a 0.1 percent decline in the overall February PPI and a 0.1 percent increase in the core rate.
The Standard & Poor's 500 index future gained 4.05 points to 802.00, indicating a 30 to 35 point Dow rise at the open.
